cards.name: Lighting Effects
cards.summary: Relights the clip with up to five virtual lights (spot, omni or directional) plus an ambient level, darkening everything the lights do not reach. Can also emboss a texture via a bump layer.
use_for: Spotlight one leader in a group press photo while the rest falls dark
Add a warm pool of light to a flat, evenly lit interview or archive still
Moody low-key look for documentary reenactments and trailer title backdrops
Slow light sweep across a still image to give it life in an explainer
avoid: Defaults (Ambience Intensity 20) darken the whole frame a lot: raise Ambience Intensity if only a subtle relight is wanted
Hard-edged spot (high Focus) on a face looks like a cheap stage light
Bump Layer needs another track and is not settable from a spec

params.name: Light Type
params.does: Light 1 type dropdown (Light Type#2..#5 for lights 2-5, which default to None)

params.name: Center
params.does: Where light 1 is aimed, frame fractions

params.name: Major Radius
params.does: Long radius of the spotlight ellipse (% of frame)

params.name: Minor Radius
params.does: Short radius of the ellipse

params.name: Intensity
params.does: Brightness of light 1

params.name: Focus
params.does: Size of the bright core inside the light ellipse; higher = fuller, flatter pool with a more abrupt edge, lower = small hotspot with long falloff (direction not render-verified)

params.name: Light Color
params.does: Colour of light 1

params.name: Ambience Intensity
params.does: Brightness of the unlit areas (ambient fill)

cards.scripting: Each of the five lights repeats the same property names: light 1 = 'Light Type', 'Center', 'Intensity'...; light 2 = 'Light Type#2', 'Center#2'...; up to #5. 'Light 1'..'Light 5' bools and the unnamed bools are group rows, do not set them. Only light 1 is on by default (Light Type 3); set 'Light Type#2' etc. to a non-zero value to add lights. 'Bump Layer' is a track picker whose harvested range is garbage (min > max): never set it. Angle is in degrees. Ambience Intensity below ~10 or light Intensity above ~60 tends to crush the surround or blow out the hotspot; check a frame. Light Type labels (None/Directional/Omni/Spotlight) follow the Premiere UI order, medium confidence.

verified.note: Warm spotlight pool lights the upper-left of the frame while the right side and frame edges fall darker, as described.

cards.name: Lightning
cards.summary: Draws an animated electric bolt between a start and end point on top of the clip, with branches, glow colours and random flicker.
use_for: Electric 'connection' line between two faces or logos in a satire or explainer graphic
Storm or power hit on a trailer title card
One-frame-to-few-frames energy flash on a hook beat
Comic 'shock' accent when a claim is busted in a political reel
avoid: Left on for long it looks like 2000s stock FX on real footage; keep it to short hits
Thin defaults (Width 10) are hard to see at 1080p
Outside Color is harvested as a broken number and cannot be set from a spec

params.name: Start point
params.does: Where the bolt starts, frame fractions

params.name: End point
params.does: Where the bolt ends

params.name: Segments
params.does: Number of zig-zag segments of the main bolt

params.name: Amplitude
params.does: How far the bolt wanders from a straight line

params.name: Branching
params.does: Amount of side branches (0-1)

params.name: Width
params.does: Bolt thickness

params.name: Speed
params.does: How fast the bolt shape changes

params.name: Inside Color
params.does: Core colour of the bolt

cards.scripting: Points are frame fractions. 'Outside Color' was harvested as a number with an invalid range (min > max): it is really a colour, so do not set it from a spec. 'Blending Mode' is a 0..2 dropdown, default 1; the Normal/Add/Screen labels come from the old AE Lightning (same plug-in, 3 items) and are not render-verified. The bolt animates on its own with time; 'Rerun At Each Frame' true gives a completely new bolt every frame (harsh flicker). Animate opacity or trim the clip to make short hits.

verified.note: A white-core, blue-glow branching bolt crosses the frame from upper left to the right foreground block on top of the clip.

cards.name: Linear Wipe (Legacy)
cards.summary: In-clip wipe effect that makes the clip transparent along a straight edge at a chosen angle, revealing the track below as Transition Completion rises. Still renders but is the legacy version.
use_for: Wipe a top-track clip on or off over the clip below without a transition
Static diagonal split screen of two leaders (completion ~50, feathered)
Reveal a map or graphic from left to right in an explainer
avoid: On a single track the revealed area is black, which looks like a mistake
Zero feather on fast moves looks cheap; add 20-100 px

params.name: Transition Completion
params.does: Percent of the clip wiped away (transparent)

params.name: Wipe Angle
params.does: Direction the wipe travels, in degrees (90 = travels left to right with a vertical edge; add 180 to reverse)

params.name: Feather
params.does: Softness of the wipe edge in pixels

cards.equivalent: Linear Wipe (video transition) for wipes on a cut; Gradient Wipe effect for in-clip reveals; AE: Linear Wipe
cards.scripting: Needs content on a lower track to show anything but black. Prefer the 'Linear Wipe' transition when the wipe sits on a cut; keep this effect only for in-clip or static split-screen use (no direct new-generation effect replacement was found in the harvest). The new transition can also sit single-sided at a clip's start/end to wipe a top clip on/off. Wipe Angle is in degrees and unbounded; which side clears first for a given angle is medium confidence (90 is believed to clear from the left), so flip by 180 if a frame check shows the wrong side.

verified.note: At completion 50 and angle 135 the upper-left half is wiped to black (transparent on a single track) along a slightly soft diagonal edge.

cards.name: Luma Key
cards.summary: Makes the dark (low-luminance) parts of a clip transparent so the track below shows through. Used to drop elements shot on black over other footage.
use_for: Lay fire, smoke, sparks or light-leak stock shot on black over footage
Drop a white-on-black logo or text plate over a shot
Add dust, film-scratch or bokeh overlays shot on black over archive footage
avoid: On a single track, keyed areas just turn black, so the effect is barely visible
Compressed stock gives noisy, chattering key edges; Screen blend mode on the clip is often cleaner for light elements
Keys dark parts of the subject too (hair, suits): not for keying people
Cannot key a white background (no invert option): for dark ink on white paper (newspaper scans, signatures) use Multiply blend mode instead

params.name: Threshold
params.does: Range of dark values that become transparent (higher = more of the image keyed)

params.name: Cutoff
params.does: Opacity of the non-keyed areas / hardness of the key (higher = more transparent)

cards.scripting: Only meaningful on an upper track over other footage; on a single track transparent = black. Defaults (Threshold 100, Cutoff 0) are believed to act as a soft luminance matte already (pure black transparent, dark tones partly see-through), not a no-op. The exact Threshold/Cutoff interaction is from Adobe's legacy docs and not verified by render: tune by eye, start Threshold 40-60, Cutoff 20-30 for elements on black; high Cutoff (60+) can make most of a normal shot transparent. Despite the match name containing 'Legacy', it is the current Luma Key in the Keying folder.

verified.note: Dark tones (block fronts, clothing, shadows) are keyed out and read as black on the single track while light areas stay intact.

cards.name: Lumetri Color
cards.summary: Premiere's main colour-grading effect: white balance, exposure and tone, creative looks and LUTs, curves, colour wheels, HSL secondary and vignette in one GPU effect.
use_for: Fix white balance and exposure of mismatched news/press footage so cuts match
Give a documentary a consistent look (contrast, slight fade, vignette)
Black-and-white or desaturated flashback for archive sections
Warm/cool emotional shift between political 'promise' and 'reality' segments
Punchy saturated grade for social reels
avoid: Saturation above ~140 pushes Indian skin tones orange and clips on YouTube
Applying a creative Look at full intensity on every shot looks templated
Crushing blacks (Blacks < -40) loses detail after platform compression

params.name: Temperature
params.does: Basic Correction white balance, blue (-) to yellow (+)

params.name: Saturation
params.does: Basic Correction saturation (100 = unchanged)

params.name: Exposure
params.does: Basic Correction exposure in stops

params.name: Contrast
params.does: Basic Correction contrast

params.name: Highlights
params.does: Recover (-) or boost (+) bright areas

params.name: Shadows
params.does: Lift (+) or deepen (-) shadows

params.name: Faded Film
params.does: Creative: lifts blacks for a faded film look

params.name: Amount
params.does: Vignette amount (negative darkens edges)

cards.scripting: Names repeat across sections: 'Saturation' = Basic, 'Saturation#2' = Creative, 'Saturation#3' = HSL Secondary correction; 'Temperature'/'Tint'/'Contrast' = Basic, '#2' = HSL Secondary; 'Intensity#2' = Creative Look intensity; 'Sharpen' = Creative; 'Amount', 'Midpoint', 'Roundness', 'Feather' = Vignette. The 'Active', 'Active#2'..'Active#13' bools are section and sub-curve enable switches in panel order ('Active' = Basic Correction, '#2' = Creative, '#3' = Curves, '#10' = Color Wheels, '#11' = HSL Secondary, '#12' = Vignette): leave true. 'Intensity' (first, 0-100, default 50) sits in Basic Correction before the Color group and is unidentified: do not set it. Section-name bools (Basic Correction, Creative, Curves, Vignette...) are group rows: do not set. Harvested numeric ranges are wider than the UI sliders (Temperature/Tint +-300, Contrast etc. +-150, Exposure +-7, vignette Amount +-5) so stay near UI ranges. Look and Input LUT are 0-based dropdowns over the installed LUT list (0 = None); other indices depend on the install, and custom .cube files (LUTAsset/LookAsset strings), curves, colour wheels and HSL keys are blobs that cannot be set from a spec: use a saved effect preset for those.

verified.note: Frame is warmer, more saturated and contrastier, with visibly darkened vignette corners.

cards.name: Magnify (Legacy)
cards.summary: Draws a circular or square magnifying-glass zoom of part of the image, with feather, opacity and blend controls. Still renders but is the legacy version.
use_for: Magnify a line in a document, tweet or newspaper clip in an explainer
Callout a face or badge in a wide crowd/press photo
Animated loupe sweeping over a chart or map
avoid: High magnification on low-res stills looks blurry and cheap
No outline: add a stroke/shape ring if it must read as a magnifier
Centred on a flat area (plain wall, sky) the loupe is nearly invisible: aim Center at a face, text or other detail

params.name: Shape
params.does: Circle or square lens

params.name: Center
params.does: Where the lens sits, frame fractions

params.name: Magnification
params.does: Zoom inside the lens in percent

params.name: Size
params.does: Lens radius in pixels

params.name: Feather
params.does: Softness of the lens edge in pixels

params.name: Link
params.does: Ties size/feather to magnification

params.name: Resize Layer
params.does: Lets the lens extend beyond the clip bounds

cards.equivalent: No new-generation Magnify found in the harvest; this legacy effect still works. Alternative: duplicate the clip, scale it with Transform/Motion and cut it with a mask. AE: Magnify
cards.scripting: Marked (Legacy) by Premiere 2026 but no direct replacement exists in this install, so it remains the simplest scripted loupe: e.g. Magnification 220, Size 250, Feather 8, Center on the detail. Enum labels come from the AE version of Magnify (same plug-in), medium confidence. 'Blending Mode' is a 0..21 dropdown (default 1, probably Normal); labels not verified. Size and Feather are pixels, not fractions.

verified.note: A circular loupe over a face shows it clearly enlarged against the unmagnified surroundings.

cards.name: Mask
cards.summary: Internal component that holds a mask drawn on a clip's effect or Opacity (ellipse, 4-point or pen mask), with feather, opacity, expansion and invert. It is created by Premiere's mask tools rather than picked from the Effects panel.
use_for: Limit a blur or mosaic to a face or number plate for censoring
Spot-grade a face with a masked Lumetri
Vignette-shaped opacity cut-out for picture-in-picture
avoid: Untracked masks drift off moving subjects
Hard (0 feather) masks on grades show visible edges

params.name: Mask Feather
params.does: Edge softness in pixels

params.name: Mask Opacity
params.does: Strength of the masked area

params.name: Mask Expansion
params.does: Grows (+) or shrinks (-) the mask in pixels

params.name: Inverted
params.does: Applies the effect outside the shape instead
params.typical: false; true for grading the background

cards.scripting: Cannot be created from a spec: 'Mask Path', 'Additional Paths' and 'Selection Data Param' are binary strings, so a script cannot draw the shape. Route: save an effect preset (.prfpset) with the mask already drawn and apply it, or build the masked shot in After Effects. Once a mask exists, feather/opacity/expansion/inverted are plain numbers/bools. Probably not listed in the Effects panel; low confidence on how scripts can reach it.

verified.note: needs_input card: no gallery frame exists (a mask cannot be drawn from a spec).
verified.second_opinion: agree: no frame exists (status needs_input, absent from gallery/pr/index.json); harvest confirms Mask Path / Additional Paths / Selection Data Param are binary strings, Feather 0..5000 (default 10), Opacity 0..100, Expansion -5000..5000, empty demo_settings is correct

cards.name: Mask2
cards.summary: Newer internal mask component (Premiere 2025/2026 masking) with its own transform (position, scale, rotation, anchor), feather, opacity, expansion, invert, blend mode, mask type and tracker data. Created by the mask tools, not from the Effects panel.
use_for: Isolate a face or object for blur/censor or a spot grade
Tracked mask following a moving subject for a highlight
Combine several shapes (add/subtract) for a custom cut-out
avoid: Tracker data does not survive being rebuilt from a script
Expecting a script to draw the path: it cannot

params.name: Feather
params.does: Edge softness

params.name: Opacity
params.does: Strength of the mask

params.name: Expansion
params.does: Grows or shrinks the mask

params.name: Inverted
params.does: Flips inside/outside

params.name: Rotation
params.does: Rotates the mask shape (degrees)

params.name: Blend Mode
params.does: How this mask combines with other masks (0..2, probably Add/Subtract/Intersect)

params.name: Type
params.does: Mask type dropdown (0..4, probably ellipse/rectangle/pen/object kinds)

cards.scripting: Path, Tracker and User Interactions are binary strings and cannot be set from a spec, so the mask must come from a saved effect preset or be drawn by hand. Position/Scale/Anchor Point units are unclear from the harvest (Position default [0, 0], Scale [1, 1]); Blend Mode and Type labels are guesses, not verified. Treat as read-mostly.

verified.note: needs_input card: no gallery frame exists (a mask cannot be drawn from a spec).
verified.second_opinion: agree: no frame exists (status needs_input, absent from gallery/pr/index.json); harvest confirms Path, two Tracker rows and User Interactions are binary strings, Position [0,0] / Scale [1,1], Rotation -32768..32767, Blend Mode 0..2, Type 0..4, Feather default 0; empty demo_settings is correct

cards.name: Metadata & Timecode Burn-in
cards.summary: Burns up to five lines of timecode or clip metadata (source/sequence timecode, clip name, file name and similar) into the picture on a semi-transparent box.
use_for: Review/approval exports for clients or legal with timecode to reference notes
Burn source timecode on interview selects for transcript logging
Show clip names on an adjustment layer for assistant-editor checks of a rough cut
avoid: Forgetting to disable it before the final export

On an adjustment layer, per-clip fields (clip name, source timecode) follow the 'Source Track' picker, which cannot be set from a spec: check the burn-in reads the intended track, or apply it to the clips themselves

params.name: Size
params.does: Overall text size

params.name: Opacity
params.does: Opacity of the background box behind the text

params.name: Metadata
params.does: Line 1 field dropdown (Metadata#2..#5 for lines 2-5)

params.name: Position
params.does: Line 1 position, frame fractions

params.name: Format
params.does: Timecode format dropdown for line 1

params.name: Time Display
params.does: Frame-rate/time display dropdown for line 1

params.name: Offset
params.does: Frame offset added to the displayed time

params.name: Size#2
params.does: Line 1 text scale in percent (per-line, on top of the global Size; meaning inferred from its 0-200 range)

cards.scripting: Five line groups repeat the same names: line 1 = 'Metadata', 'Position', 'Size#2', 'Format', 'Time Display', 'Offset', 'Starting Timecode' (number) + 'Starting Timecode#2' (bool); line 2 = 'Metadata#2', 'Position#2', 'Size#3', 'Format#2', ... 'Starting Timecode#3'/'#4'; line N uses Starting Timecode #(2N-1) number and #(2N) bool. The first 'Size' and 'Opacity' are global (text size, background box opacity). 'Line 1'..'Line 5' bools are group rows (harvested false although line 1 shows by default): do not set them. A line is shown by giving its 'Metadata#N' a non-zero value. Metadata is a 0..27 dropdown whose labels were not harvested (default 6 on line 1, 0 on lines 2-5, believed to be None). Format 0..3 is probably SMPTE / Frames / Feet+Frames 16mm / 35mm as in the Timecode effect; Time Display 0..7 labels unknown. 'Source Track' has an invalid harvested range (min > max): do not set it.

verified.note: Large white source timecode 00:00:02:00 is burned in at lower centre on a semi-opaque black box.

cards.name: Mirror
cards.summary: Reflects one side of the image onto the other across a line defined by a centre point and an angle, giving symmetrical or kaleidoscope-like frames.
use_for: Symmetrical 'two faces' or double-leader satire shots
Trippy symmetry for music reels and trailer montages
Mirror wipe transition by animating Reflection Center across the frame
Fill an empty half of a frame for a stylised background plate
avoid: Faces cut by the mirror line look disturbing: keep the line off faces unless that is the joke
Text or logos mirror backwards
Default centre [1, 0.5] sits on the right edge, so nothing visible happens

params.name: Reflection Center
params.does: A point on the mirror line, frame fractions

params.name: Reflection Angle
params.does: Angle of the mirror line in degrees (0 = vertical line, left side reflected to the right)

cards.scripting: Points are frame fractions. Stack two Mirror instances (Angle 0 and 90) for a four-way kaleidoscope. A separate 'Mirror' video transition also exists; use that on cuts. Which side is kept for a given angle should be checked by eye.

verified.note: The left half is reflected onto the right across the vertical centre line, giving a symmetrical double of the left half of the frame.

cards.name: Mosaic (Legacy)
cards.summary: Pixelates the clip into a grid of solid-colour blocks. Superseded in Premiere 2026 by the new Mosaic effect but still renders.
use_for: Censor a face, number plate or private document (with an effect mask)
Pixel-resolve reveal on a hook or title
Retro 8-bit stylisation for meme-style reels
avoid: Too many (small) blocks leave a censored face recognisable, especially in motion: keep blocks 30+ px (40-60 Horizontal Blocks on a 1920 frame, since blocks count across the whole clip even under a mask)
Unmasked full-frame mosaic for long durations tires viewers

params.name: Horizontal Blocks
params.does: Number of blocks across the whole clip (fewer = bigger blocks)

params.name: Vertical Blocks
params.does: Number of blocks down
params.typical: Horizontal Blocks / 1.78 for square blocks at 16:9

params.name: Sharp Colors
params.does: Uses the centre pixel colour instead of the block average

cards.scripting: Prefer the new 'Mosaic' effect when it is available; this legacy one is the fallback and works with simple numbers. For square blocks keep Vertical = round(Horizontal * height / width). Limiting it to a face needs an effect mask, which a script cannot draw (use a saved preset). The resolve recipe ends at 400x225 blocks (still slightly soft): cut or disable the effect right after the last keyframe.

verified.note: The whole frame is pixelated into a coarse grid of solid-colour blocks.
